title: Tampa City Council approves Rays' stadium deal in narrow 4-3 vote
dek: Tampa City Council voted 4-3 Thursday to approve the city's participation in a $2.36 billion Rays ballpark project. The deal now advances to a county vote Friday. The project anchors a mixed-use development on Hillsborough College's Dale Mabry campus.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Tampa City Council voted 4-3 to approve the city's $80 million share of a $2.36 billion Rays ballpark, advancing the decades-long stadium saga to a final county commission decision.
bottom_line: The county commission's Friday vote is the final gate on the Rays' stadium timeline. A county rejection would reset the entire process and likely resurrect stadium uncertainty for the franchise.
body: Tampa City Council voted 4-3 Thursday to approve the city's participation in a $2.36 billion Rays ballpark project, according to MLB.com. The deal now advances to a county vote Friday, per Yahoo Sports. The ballpark anchors a mixed-use development planned for Hillsborough College's Dale Mabry campus.

The narrow margin underscores the political division surrounding the stadium proposal in Tampa. The city's approval does not guarantee passage at the county level, which holds the power to approve or block the transaction.

The Rays' stadium saga spans decades. Previous stadium proposals, financing structures, and political alignments have shifted repeatedly without resolution. This vote represents the closest the franchise has come to locking in a long-term home through the formal municipal approval process.
